sections.overview: The dusky hopping mouse is a small rodent of arid inland Australia.
sections.identification: Large ears, long hind feet and a brush-tipped tail mark this hopping mouse.
sections.habitat: It occurs patchily in sandy deserts of central Australia.
sections.diet: It eats seeds, berries, leaves and other green plants, with insects only occasionally.
sections.behavior: It is nocturnal, shelters in deep burrows and forages close to them.
sections.reproduction: Little is known in the wild beyond its opportunistic breeding.
sections.ecology: Introduced foxes and cats prey on hopping mice, while grazing and rabbits can degrade the vegetation and sandy habitat on which this species depends.
sections.conservation: It is Vulnerable nationally in Australia and Endangered in New South Wales; its sparse and fragmented populations remain difficult to survey.
